walkthroughs.h2: Risk is part of the job
walkthroughs.body_html:
Every new business takes risk — it might fail.

Smart founders take calculated risks: research, plan, test small, then commit.

Reckless risk is reckless. Calculated risk is brave.

Setbacks are normal:

  • A supplier lets you down.
  • An advert flops.
  • Customers don't show up.

The trick is to learn the lesson and keep going.

A growth mindset says: 'I can't do it… yet.'

Failure isn't the end — it's the data that helps the next try.

JK Rowling was rejected 12 times before Harry Potter was published. 📚

mcqs.q: Why are cash flow and profit different on different time-scales?
options: Profit is recognised when a sale is made (even on credit); cash flow is when money actually moves. A profitable sale today may produce no cash for 60 days while bills are due — creating a cash-flow problem despite profit.
Cash flow only matters at year-end.
The 7Ps include Profit, Planning and Performance.
Cash flow and profit are the same thing measured differently.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between fixed and variable costs?
options: Cash flow only matters at year-end.
Fixed costs are paid every month and variable costs are paid weekly.
Fixed costs are the cheapest costs and variable costs are the most expensive.
Fixed costs do not change with output level (e.g. rent, salaries); variable costs change in proportion to output (e.g. raw materials, hourly wages).
